title: Isolation of Symbiodiniaceae from Coral Hosts for Cryopreservation and Laser-Warming
author: Jessica Bouwmeester
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.b4e3qtgn

steps.title: Sample Selection and Baseline Measurement
steps.instruction: Select 3-5 genotypes for each target species to ensure a representative sample of the Symbiodiniaceae commonly found in that species. Measure the photosynthetic yield of each genotype using a PAM fluorometer as a reference control value.

steps.title: Coral Tissue Blasting
steps.instruction: Blast coral tissue containing algal endosymbionts from the skeleton using a dental flosser filled with filtered seawater (FSW). Collect the blastate (tissue and symbionts in FSW) in a bowl or Ziploc bag, aiming for 250-900 mL total.

substeps.instruction: For mushroom corals (e.g., Lobactis scutaria), avoid the polyp mouth to minimize mucus and allow fungiid recovery.

steps.title: Initial Filtration for Brittle Skeletons
steps.instruction: For corals with brittle skeletons (e.g., some Pocillopora and Acropora species), filter the blastate through a 200-µm filter to exclude skeleton shards.

steps.title: Initial Centrifugation and Homogenization
steps.instruction: Distribute the blastate (including mucus) into 50-mL falcon tubes, balancing volumes using a transfer pipette. Centrifuge the tubes for 10 min at RCF = 2300 x g.

substeps.instruction: For each tube, transfer the floating raft into a 15-mL glass tissue grinder.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 1-2 mL FSW using a 1-mL pipette and add it to the floating raft in the grinder.
Add FSW and homogenize the contents using a loose pestle until the solution is homogeneous.

steps.title: First Filtration Stage (200-µm)
steps.instruction: Transfer the homogenized solution through a 200-µm filter into a glass beaker. Repeat the centrifugation and homogenization process for all 50-mL tubes used.

steps.title: Second Centrifugation and Homogenization
steps.instruction: Transfer the filtered solution into clean 50-mL falcon tubes (maximum 6 tubes). Measure the photosynthetic yield in one tube using a PAM fluorometer to ensure symbiont health. Centrifuge the tubes for 10 min at RCF = 2300 x g.

substeps.instruction: Discard the supernatant for each tube.
Resuspend the pellet in 1-2 mL FSW using a 1-mL pipette.
Transfer all resuspended pellets to a clean glass tissue grinder.
Add FSW if needed and homogenize with a loose pestle until homogeneous.

steps.title: Sequential Filtration and Purification
steps.instruction: Perform a series of filtration, centrifugation, and homogenization steps to further purify the symbionts. For each of the following filter sizes, follow the same cycle: filter the solution, measure photosynthetic yield with a Junior PAM fluorometer, centrifuge for 10 min at RCF = 2300 x g, discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 1-2 mL FSW, and homogenize in a glass tissue grinder.

substeps.instruction: Filter through 100-µm filter into clean 50-mL tubes (aim for 1-2 tubes).
Filter through 70-µm filter into a clean 50-mL tube (aim for 1 tube).
Filter through 40-µm filter into a clean 50-mL tube (aim for 1 tube).
Filter through 20-µm filter into a clean 50-mL tube (aim for a final volume of 50 mL / 1 tube).

steps.title: Culture Preparation and Incubation
steps.instruction: Prepare an Erlenmeyer flask with 50 mL of double-strength Guillard’s F2 Marine Enrichment Solution containing double-strength Polne-Fuller antibiotic cocktail. Gently add the Symbiodiniaceae solution while swirling until the total volume is 100 mL.

substeps.instruction: Close the flask opening with filter paper or a circle of fine mesh fabric and secure with a rubber band.
Place in an incubator overnight at 24-26°C with a day/night light cycle.

steps.title: Final Purification and Recovery
steps.instruction: The next morning, resuspend the solution using a 1-mL or transfer pipette and pour into 2-3 50-mL falcon tubes. Centrifuge for 10 min at RCF = 2300 x g.

substeps.instruction: Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 1-2 mL FSW using a 1-mL pipette.
Transfer pellets to a clean glass tissue grinder, add FSW if needed, and homogenize with a loose pestle.
Transfer the homogenized solution through a 20-µm filter into a clean 50-mL tube (aim for max 50 mL / 1 tube).
Take a final photosynthetic yield measurement using a Junior PAM fluorometer.

steps.title: Storage and Usage
steps.instruction: The Symbiodiniaceae solution is now ready. Depending on community composition, it remains stable for 2-3 days.

substeps.instruction: For immediate use: Use as is.
For use later in the day: Dilute to 50 mL in FSW.
For use on a later day: Dilute to 100 mL in an Erlenmeyer flask in Guillard’s F2 Marine Enrichment Solution.
